prompt.brief: Design a privacy-aware product analytics pipeline that collects user events, computes near-real-time and historical reports, supports flexible dimensions, and remains cost-efficient at billions of events per day.
successSignals: Define an event schema, identity stitching, consent, bot filtering, deduplication, late-arrival policy, retention, and tenant isolation.
Separate immutable raw events from streaming rollups and warehouse queries; support new dimensions without rewriting the ingestion contract.
Explain approximate distinct counts, attribution windows, backfills, replay, schema evolution, dashboard freshness, and cost controls.
Cover access control, deletion propagation, sampling, data quality, observability, and degraded reporting.

functional: Collect page views, clicks, sessions, conversions, and custom events from web/mobile clients with validation and retry-safe ingestion.
Provide funnels, cohorts, retention, paths, real-time counters, segmentation, export, and scheduled reports with freshness metadata.
Support consent withdrawal, user deletion, schema versions, replay/backfill, correction of late events, and tenant-scoped access.
nonFunctional: Publish common real-time aggregates within one minute while retaining raw-event durability for exact historical recomputation.
Scale to billions of events per day and high-cardinality tenants without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5B events/day, 100k events/second peak, and 100k dashboard users
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Privacy-aware product analytics pipeline latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
